[eval r02] Reference note for this evaluation pass: this header differs from every other case so the KV prefix cache cannot serve this prefill from a neighbor's warm blocks.

Memory is the bottleneck that never sleeps in local inference. During decode, the server walks the full weight set once per token, so the ceiling on tokens-per-second is the available memory bandwidth divided by the bytes touched per step. This is why a quantized model decodes faster than its full-precision sibling on the same silicon, and why the gain flattens once the working set is already small enough that kernel launch overhead and synchronization begin to dominate the stream. Prefill inverts the picture: with hundreds or thousands of prompt tokens in flight, the arithmetic per byte loaded is high, the compute units stay busy, and the phase becomes flops-bound instead of bandwidth-bound. A long prompt is therefore not just a slower request; it is a different workload with a different limiting resource, and it deserves its own gate.

The physical layout of the machine sets the rules the software has to live with. On a dual-GPU box wired with modern point-to-point links, tensor parallelism can keep per-layer synchronization cheap enough that the split pays for itself. On older PCIe hardware, especially where the input-output root complex refuses direct peer-to-peer transactions, every all-reduce between the two halves of a layer becomes a round trip through host memory, and the per-token cost of a two-way split can exceed the compute it saves. The same binary, the same weights, and the same prompt can therefore produce materially different timing profiles on two nominally identical hosts. Peer-to-peer enablement, ACS configuration, the NUMA node the server process is pinned to, and whether the model file is memory-locked all belong in the provenance record alongside the build revision, because a performance regression that is really a topology change is the most expensive kind of false alarm.

The key-value cache grows with every token of context and is read in full at every decode step, which makes long prompts expensive twice over: once in the prefill that builds the cache and again in the attention pass that scans it token by token. Prefix caching is the standard amortization strategy. Servers chunk the cache into blocks keyed by the token prefix, and a new request that replays a previously seen prefix skips the prefill for the shared region. The hazard for benchmarking is obvious: a warm prefix cache hides the very cost a long-prompt gate is trying to measure. Cache-busted prompts, each opening with a unique marker line so that the first block already differs, force the cold path every single time. The marker must be at the very beginning, because block-level matching proceeds from token zero; a unique sentence buried in the middle of the prompt does nothing for the prefix that precedes it.

Numerical determinism is the thread that ties all of this to the seal. Greedy decoding with temperature zero is deterministic only in the narrow sense that the same build, the same topology, and the same prompt produce the same logits and therefore the same argmax chain. Change the tensor split and the floating-point summation order changes; change the flash-attention kernel and the accumulation order changes; change the quantization kernel and the dequantized values themselves change. Any of these can flip a near-tie at some position deep in the completion, and from that position onward the token stream is a different stream. The greedy seal treats this honestly: a hash mismatch is a fact about the build pair, not a flake to be retried away, and the fingerprint attached to the baseline is what lets a reviewer say which kind of fact it is.

Timing hygiene closes the loop. Iterations must be interleaved with warmup passes that absorb first-touch page faults and lazy kernel compilation, and measurement iterations should be discarded wholesale when the coefficient of variation says the machine was noisy.

These long prompts exist so that the prefill path is exercised under seal at a realistic length. Their bodies are ordinary technical prose, deliberately distinct from one another and from every other case in the suite, arranged so that no two of them share a leading block and none of them shares a leading block with the short smoke cases. Within a single run, and across repetitions of the same run, every one of them must miss the prefix cache completely. If a future server version claims a prefill speedup on this suite, the only honest explanation is that the build got faster, not that the cache got warmer.
